paper_title: New Limits on Exotic Spin-Dependent Interactions at Astronomical Distances
notes: MonopoleDipole (SP) scalar-pseudoscalar coupling product |g_S^N g_P^n| between polarized neutron and unpolarized nucleons (nucleon-nucleon), the paper's headline result (abstract: surpasses combined astro-lab limits, most stringent to date). Extracted from Fig.2 (fig2.eps -> PDF, pymupdf get_drawings, vector). Fig.2 x-axis is interaction range lambda in metres; converted to boson mass via m=hbar c/lambda=1.97327e-7 eV*m/lambda (consistent with the figure's own top mass axis). y-axis is |g_S^N g_P^n| (dimensionless product), read directly. Curve is the lower envelope of the two 'This work' solid curves: 'using the Moon' (drawing idx5, covers small lambda/large mass) and 'using the Sun' (drawing idx3, most stringent, reaches plateau 1.6e-35 for lambda>1e12 m i.e. mass<2e-19 eV). Crossover at lambda~2e10 m (mass~1e-17 eV) matches the paper's statement that the Sun gives the most stringent limit for lambda>=2e10 m. Dashed 'Astro Limit' (drawing idx4, from Refs) excluded. Not a DM search (Sun/Moon source mass + Earth-rotation sidereal modulation), so dm_density null. 95% C.L. per Eq.9/text. Couplings dimensionless products; no 2m_N rescaling applies. VA (g_V^N g_A^n, Fig.3) and AA (g_A^N g_A^n, Fig.4) are secondary results not reported here.
